Embattled Fifa president Gianni Infantino has apologised for “mistakes” over his controversial World Cup sell-off plan but senior leaders at world football’s governing body have “reaffirm[ed] their full support” for him after a crisis meeting on Wednesday.

Infantino was forced to abandon his plans – namely to sell stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa tournaments to private investors – after public uproar last week, with Uefa confirming a boycott of Fifa events if the plan was voted through.

On Tuesday, Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused Infantino of “blackmail” and, under immense pressure, with his job seemingly on the line, the Swiss-Italian called an emergency meeting with the Fifa management board in Morocco.

open image in gallery Gianni Infantino has retained the support of Fifa ( PA Wire )

A letter released by Fifa on Wednesday evening was signed by both Infantino and Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, even though the latter is understood to have written an email to staff on Tuesday in which he described Infantino’s proposal as “sad and reproachable”.

It showed a far more united front than that email would suggest and saw the president admits that mistakes were made in the process of setting out his sell-off plans – his first public apology for the scheme.

“We acknowledge mistakes were made in the process of the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE),” read part of the letter.

“It was certainly not the intention for the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations to feel excluded from the process and it should have been handled differently. We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again. With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.”

open image in gallery Infantino did say mistakes were made in the process of the World Cup sell-off plan ( PA Wire )

However, any suggestion that Infantino might resign, or otherwise be forced out of his job by senior figures at the governing body, were also nipped in the bud with a clear show of support for the embattled president.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the FIFA Secretary General and the Management Board in attendance reaffirm their full support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations,” read part of the statement.

“It was discussed and agreed at the meeting that the processes, communications and interactions between the FIFA President, the FIFA Secretary General and the Management Board that support the delivery of this vision can and should always be continuously improved in terms of their effectiveness and efficiency.

“We are fully confident that the outcomes of today's meeting will strengthen FIFA's governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner while continuing our mission to develop the game around the world.”

The statement also went on to say that any attacks on Fifa’s integrity or good governance will not be accepted and seemed to suggest that now the sell-off plan has been abandoned, the whole situation should be quietly forgotten.

open image in gallery Infantino also said attacks on Fifa’s integrity would not be tolerated ( PA )

”The proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table,” read another part of the statement. “With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

“There are always lessons to be learned, and we will continue to improve our processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done, was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework.”

Infantino still faces a barrage of criticism from outside Fifa however, with a number of countries having withdrawn support for his presidency ahead of the election in March 2027.

Real Madrid and Portugal legend Luis Figo, who works as an adviser for Uefa, hit out at Infantino on Wednesday and implored him to resign, saying: “I could write 10,000 words on the problems at Fifa. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go.”

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney also said he no longer has confidence Infantino, explaining he felt the Fifa president committed a “fatal” governance failure by not consulting senior advisers. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr Infantino,” said Carney, who had appeared alongside Infantino at several events during the 2026 World Cup co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States.

Yvette Cooper has announced new fast-track support for motor neurone disease (MND) patients, forming part of a wider overhaul of social care.

The Health Secretary paid tribute to the late Rob Burrow, the former England rugby league star who died in 2024 from MND complications.

Visiting a Leeds care centre named after Mr Burrow, Ms Cooper highlighted his crucial work in raising awareness and improving support for those affected, also acknowledging the efforts of his family and former teammate Sir Kevin Sinfield.

She said: “What we’ve got to do now is make sure the principles that apply here about supporting families and patients are applied throughout the National Health Service and also in our social care system too.

“That’s why when Andy Burnham set out a vision for a National Care Service, we prioritised MND as being something we should focus on now, providing social care support for affected families and speeding it up as well.”

Kevin Sinfield, left, and Rob Burrow, pictured in 2023, campaigned to raise millions of pounds and raise awareness of MND ( Danny Lawson/PA )

The new fast-track pathway is intended to tackle “delays and fragmentation” in support for those with MND as part of the “first phase” of fixing the social care system, the Department for Health and Social Care said.

It will be developed alongside the Motor Neurone Disease Association, existing patients and carers, and others working in health, social care and housing.

Tanya Curry, chief executive of the MND Association, said: “We hear time and time again of people with MND forced to battle a system that is slow, disjointed and too complex to move quickly enough to support people with a rapidly progressing disease.

“This must change – Ms Cooper’s statement today suggests she agrees and that there is willingness at the highest levels of Government to transform the experience for people with MND.

“We must now see that willingness turned into action, with real solutions implemented nationally and locally, in health and social care.”

The announcement comes a week after the Prime Minister pledged to work with other parties to reform the social care system, describing the current situation as “bad for everybody”.

Mr Burnham announced he would be expediting Baroness Louise Casey’s commission into social care, bringing forward the original 2028 deadline to next year.

He also vowed to immediately begin reforming the workforce – saying staff should also be integrated with the NHS – as well as promising to work with the other major parties to reach a consensus on the issue.

Newcastle United have officially confirmed Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach.

The 38-year-old, who succeeds Eddie Howe, has already joined the squad at their La Manga pre-season training camp after his paperwork was finalised.

The club are understood to have paid the former Al-Ahli boss over £9 million in compensation to secure his services.

The former RB Salzburg boss said: “It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United. This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

“When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice. The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be. I have followed the club’s journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see.”

Jaissle arrives at St James’ Park with a promising pedigree having guided Salzburg to back-to-back Austrian titles before heading for the Saudi Pro League in 2023 and winning successive Asian Champions League crowns with Al-Ahli.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Newcastle’s majority owner, bought a controlling share in four Pro League clubs, including Al-Ahli, in 2023.

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson said: “Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I’m thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United.

“We have conducted a thorough process, and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role. He possesses all the qualities we were looking for.”

Jaissle has big shoes to fill on Tyneside following Howe’s decision to step down from his role on Friday after almost five years in charge.

open image in gallery Jaissle replaces Eddie Howe in the Newcastle dugout ( Getty )

The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins in November 2021 just weeks after Amanda Staveley’s consortium had completed its takeover, and aided by a significant cash injection he dragged the Magpies back from the brink of relegation from the Premier League.

In the process, he restored the connection between the fans and the club and created an optimism which was rewarded by a return to Champions League football and a first major domestic trophy in 70 years when they lifted the Carabao Cup in March 2025.

However, Howe departed after a difficult 2025-26 campaign, which was derailed before a ball had been kicked by Alexander Isak’s defection to Liverpool.

This summer’s departures of Kieran Trippier, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali – and the reported likely exit of skipper Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal – have left the squad in a state of flux.

Jaissle faces the task of steadying the ship off the pitch before Newcastle open the new campaign at home to Liverpool on August 23.

He added: “I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

“There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.”

Ed Miliband has hailed the UK and US as the "closest of allies" following talks in Washington, where he was pressed on his past criticisms of Donald Trump.

The Foreign Secretary met with Marco Rubio at the US State Department, thanking him for a "warm, productive meeting" and emphasising the strong transatlantic ties, including their roles as Nato members.

Mr Rubio, however, offered a notably less effusive account of the discussions, making no reference to the "special relationship" and merely outlining the topics covered.

Earlier, Mr Miliband chose to ignore questions about whether he still believed Donald Trump was an "idiot, a racist and a misogynist".

open image in gallery The Foreign Secretary ducked shouted inquiries by reporters about his previous strident views on Mr Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Smiling as he shook hands with Mr Rubio, the Foreign Secretary ducked shouted inquiries by reporters about his previous strident views on Mr Trump, and said: “We are looking forward to our meeting.”

Mr Miliband was invited to the US capital by Mr Rubio after their recent first meeting on the sidelines of a foreign ministers’ summit in the Philippines last month.

The pair were due to discuss efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the Ukraine war and the situation in Gaza.

The dynamic between the two men was closely watched as the White House was also reported to be concerned about Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s decision to hand Mr Miliband the Foreign Office brief.

In his previous role as energy secretary, Mr Miliband was a strong champion of net zero and renewables, while Mr Trump is a vocal supporter of fossil fuels, including opening up North Sea oil, and an avowed opponent of “windmills”.

Since arriving in Downing Street, Mr Burnham has signalled a shift in energy policy, earning praise from the Oval Office.

open image in gallery Mr Miliband was invited to the US capital by Mr Rubio after their recent first meeting on the sidelines of a foreign ministers’ summit in the Philippines last month ( Reuters )

Washington’s ambassador to the UK Warren Stephens said recently that Mr Miliband had been “wrong” in 2016 to call Mr Trump “a racist, misogynistic, self-confessed groper” and that “hopefully his views have changed”.

He also pledged to work with Mr Miliband in his new role, despite their disagreement on green issues.

In a statement after the meeting, Mr Miliband said: “Thank you to Secretary Marco Rubio for our warm, productive meeting in DC today.

“The UK and US are the closest of allies, bound by culture, history, and interests, including our shared commitment as Nato allies.

“We discussed the vital importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which is essential to protecting British families and businesses on the cost of living, this Government’s number one priority.”

The strategic sea route, which had been open before the US and Israel launched the war in February, has been a flashpoint in the Middle East conflict and disruption to trade has driven up fuel and food prices.

Mr Miliband added: “We also discussed standing together with Ukraine in the face of Putin’s war, and spoke about the intolerable situation in Gaza and the urgent need to address the humanitarian situation there, as we work towards a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis.”

Meanwhile, Mr Rubio posted pictures of himself with Mr Miliband on X and wrote: “In my meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, we discussed the need for Europe to take a greater role in its own security.

“We also reaffirmed our shared commitment to open transit in the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon.”

Separately, after the announcement that Mr Miliband will take the UK’s seat on the World Bank board, he will also meet its president Ajay Banga during his visit to discuss development, climate change and strengthening global resilience.

News.title: ​Arteta’s dynasty dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Arsenal were made to pay for a sloppy first-half display as they fell to 3-1 pre-season defeat to Spanish side Real Betis in Dublin.

All four of the game’s goals came in the first half as Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, made the Premier League champions look rusty.

Rodrigo Riquelme opened the scoring in the ninth minute. A corner from the left should have been dealt with by Kepa Arrizabalaga but the Arsenal keeper made an absolute mess of it, the ball going straight through him to Riquelme at the far post who took one touch before firing into the net.

Betis doubled their lead in the 26th minute with an absolute screamer. Nelson Deossa received the ball in a central position around 25 yards out, took a couple of touches before lashing his shot into the top corner.

Arsenal pulled a goal back in the 32nd minute when Piero Hincapié nodded in from inside the six-yard box. But 11 minutes later the Spanish side, who finished fifth in La Liga last season, reclaimed their two-goal advantage through former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals.

Mikel Arteta made a raft of second-half substitutions in a bid to turn the match around, but Betis held firm.

More to follow...

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting

Gianni Infantino has been under fire for the last week after FIFA's controversial plan to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors came to light

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to apologise (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Grovelling Gianni Infantino has apologised for attempting to sell the World Cup, confirming that the controversial plan has been SCRAPPED. Infantino has faced intense backlash since FIFA announced last week - after media reports broke the news - a proposal for its competitions to be sold to private investors, sparking anger among the football community at all levels.

‌



UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments if the plan was allowed to go ahead, while FIFA chief Arsene Wenger spoke out against it. A crisis meeting was held in Morocco on Wednesday amid the unrelenting criticism and constant leaks regarding the plans.

‌



And now Infantino has admitted defeat with an apology - although he plans to fight on and remain FIFA President, despite widespread calls for him to resign. A letter signed by both Infantino and the FIFA General Secretary, Mattias Grafstrom, reads: "We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

‌



"We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again. With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting."

The letter adds that Grafstrom and FIFA's Management Board 'reaffirm their full support' for Infantino, who's up for re-election next March. It goes on to say: "With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."

‌



Meanwhile, FIFA say that its leadership held a constructive and positive meeting in Rabat. It comes after a bombshell report claiming that Infantino had offered Morocco the chance to host 2030 World Cup final - which they're co-hosting with Spain and Portugal - if they agreed to his plan.

Should Gianni Infantino resign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images FIFA's plan to sell off the World Cup has been scrapped (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Any federations who backed the scheme were told that they would receive £30million, a portion of which would be available in January if they responded positively by a September deadline. Infantino was even accused of bribery by the president of the Jordan FA, who hit out on social media.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein posted: "We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."

Sports.title: Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 1-3 REAL BETIS: The Gunners were convincingly beaten in Dublin, giving Mikel Arteta some cause for concern ahead of his team's season which starts in just 11 days' time

View 5 Images Mikel Arteta will be disappointed with Arsenal's result and performance (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Lacklustre Arsenal fell to a comprehensive 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in their second pre-season friendly. The Gunners gave their fans in Dublin little to enjoy with an under-par display.

‌



Mikel Arteta watched his side make a string of mistakes, showing the kind of rustiness that he'll hope will be gone in less than a fortnight when they start the 2026-27 season against Manchester City for the Community Shield. Arsenal found themsleves 2-0 down inside 26 minutes and Arteta was visibly frustrated on the touchline.

‌



Piero Hincapie pulled one back but Betis didn't take long to restore their two-goal advantage before half-time. A raft of changes didn't make much difference in the second half and it was a match that will have fans talking for the wrong reasons.

‌



Here are five talking points from the Aviva Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow READ MORE :

1. Kepa's clangers

With Illan Meslier through the door, there's competition to be Arsenal's No.2 goalkeeper. But Kepa Arrizabalaga didn't help his case by making an error in the ninth minute.

‌



A corner was floated in by Pablo Fornals and Kepa came steaming out looking to punch. But the Spaniard got it all wrong and completely missed the ball, giving Rodrigo Riquelme a tap-in.

Kepa's appeals for a foul fell on deaf ears and soon enough he made another error. His poor clearance surrendered possession to Betis and Nelson Deossa punished him with an unstoppable strike.

Will Arsenal win the Premier League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Arsenal got off to a nightmare start (Image: Evan Treacy/Getty Images)

2. Still Set Piece FC

After finding themselves 2-0 down and playing poorly, Arsenal needed a response. That came in the form of - you guessed it - a corner.

New signing Christos Tzolis whipped the ball in and it evaded flapping Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles inside his own six-yard box. Standing a matter of inches from the line, Hincapie had a simple task to nod the ball in.

‌



It was another well-worked routine from the Gunners. Tzolis' delivery dipped perfectly and Betis were bamboozled by the runners in yellow, who were sporting Arsenal's new third kit.

View 5 Images Piero Hincapie pulled a goal back from a corner (Image: Paul Faith/AFP via Getty Images)

3. Guimaraes required

On the day Arsenal agreed a £75million deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, their second-choice midfield was exposed. Sloppy, lethargic, careless - all of those could be thrown at the trio of Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Kai Havertz.

‌



Both Betis' second and third goals summed up their performances that will remind the Arsenal board just why they're buying Guimaraes. Deossa's strike may've been a screamer but he was afforded was too much time to pull the trigger.

And then for Fornals' goal which restored Betis' two-goal cushion, Havertz gave the ball away with a weak pass. It was all far too easy and so unlike Arsenal.

View 5 Images Kai Havertz's mistake proved costly (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

‌



4. Injury blow for teenager

Arteta rung in the changes at half-time, making a total of seven substitutions. One who came on was Louie Copley, who captained Arsenal's under-21 side last season aged 19.

But sadly for the highly-rated midfielder, who was used at right-back, his night only last 10 minutes. Copley had landed awkwardly while chasing the ball and immediately looked in pain.

Arteta reluctantly subbed him, as the teenager had to be helped off the pitch as he struggled to put weight on his leg. Hopefully for Copley, it's nothing serious.

‌



View 5 Images Louie Copley succumbed to injury 10 minutes after coming on (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

5. Arteta managing minutes

As the game petered out, albeit with Betis looking the more likely to score against a youth Arsenal XI, Arteta made two intriguing substitutions. Gabriel Magalhaes and Gabriel Martinelli had only entered the fray at half-time, but they came off 30 minutes later.

The two Brazilians had only reached the round of 16 at the World Cup, but it's clear that Arteta is being careful with his starters who played a mammoth amount of minutes last season. Both Gabriels should be involved on Saturday at home to Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.content:
Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe

Newcastle quickly identified Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as their top target to replace Eddie Howe, but the announcement of his appointment was delayed - until now

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has been confirmed by Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Newcastle have finally confirmed the appointment of Matthias Jaissle as their new manager. Jaissle, 38, arrives from Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, with Newcastle paying a £9.5million compensation fee.

‌



The German replaces Eddie Howe, who shockingly resigned midway through pre-season last week. Jaissle has already been working with Newcastle's squad in La Manga, Spain for the last few days.

‌



But Al-Ahli wanted to delay the announcement until 7pm on Wednesday. Jaissle spent three years in Saudi Arabia following spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering in Austria.

‌



The 38-year-old guided Al-Ahli - who are owned by Newcastle's owners, the Saudi Public Investment Fund - to winning the Asian Champions League in each of the last two seasons. But Jaissle has decided to move to St James' Park, kicking off a new era.

‌



"I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see. I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

Sports.content:
Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow

Real Madrid are continuing to hold talks with Vinicius Jr and his entourage, while Arsenal are waiting in the wings hoping to pull off a sensational transfer swoop

View 2 Images Arsenal are going all out to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Real Madrid have made Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer in a bid to fend off interest from Arsenal. Vinicius, 26, has entered the final year of his current deal in Madrid and the Gunners are willing to offer him a lucrative move to London.

‌



Arsenal would be willing to make the Brazilian their highest-paid player and boss Mikel Arteta is believed to have spoken to him. On Wednesday, talks between Vinicius' camp, Real general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place.

‌



The two parties had previously been far apart in negotiations, with Vinicius demanding an eye-watering salary of €28m (£24m). According to The Athletic, Real have now raised their offer to a level which they believe reflects the forward's importance.

‌



Vinicius' decision on the proposal will either bring an end to the saga over his future or let it rumble on. Should no agreement be found, Real would have to decide whether to sell him this summer or risk letting him leave as a free agent next year.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌

If Vinicius does stay at the La Liga giants, he'll be owed a substantial loyalty bonus which is reportedly worth around £9m. New Real manager Jose Mourinho wants the 26-year-old to stay, as he aims to make a successful return to the Bernabeu.

Sports.content:
Arsenal 'prepare second offer' for England star as Morgan Rogers deal causes complication

Arsenal are looking to formalise their pursuit of a third marquee signing of the summer window in addition to Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jr

Sports.title: Rockets march on after easy win while Buttler makes history in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets extended their lead at the top of The Hundred table with a near-perfect performance that secured their fifth win in six games, leaving Birmingham Phoenix rooted to the bottom.

Sam Billings' unbeaten 31 sealed a scrappy chase after Phoenix stuttered to 111-6 despite Joe Clarke's 50, while Jos Buttler made history for the Manchester Super Giants as he became the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time.

After the Rockets elected to field, Will Smeed broke an unwanted record by being the first batter in The Hundred history to be unbeaten without scoring at the end of the powerplay. 25 runs came from that powerplay for the loss of Mitch Owen to Mohammad Amir, who had to leave the field with a strained hamstring immediately after taking the wicket.

Smeed eventually fell for six off 16 balls, with the visitors appearing tentative against a disciplined attack led by outstanding performances from spinners Calvin Harrison and Mitch Santner, along with Lewis Gregory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A crowd member made a great catch during Trent Rockets match against Birmingham Phoenix

Only Joe Clarke, Phoenix's leading run-scorer this season, managed to break free, reaching a half-century from 37 balls before finishing with 62 off 47. He became the fourth victim of Craig Overton's safe hands, with the catches setting a competition record. Of the remaining batters, only Laurie Evans reached double figures as Phoenix limped to an underwhelming 111-6 from their 100 balls.

After Amir's departure, skipper Billings had juggled his bowlers expertly as he searches for a fourth successive title in The Hundred. And when the Rockets batted, there was little pressure on the openers, Ben Duckett and Finn Allen progressing smoothly to 29-0 in the powerplay.

Mystery spinner Usman Tariq removed Duckett for 22 and delivered his customary bow celebration, conceding just six runs from his first 10 balls. However, there were simply not enough runs on the board, with 113 becoming the lowest total ever successfully defended in The Hundred men's competition.

Nye Donald came and went after a typically pugnacious six-ball 17, before Allen and Billings calmly rotated the strike at around a run a ball. Two successive sixes from Billings off Saqib Mahmood, including an outrageous slog sweep, accelerated the finish, and the result was all but confirmed when Allen holed out to Tariq at short mid-on for 28 with only six runs required.

The Rockets completed the victory with another Billings six, winning with 17 balls to spare to be sitting pretty with two games to come, their route direct to the final having got that bit easier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton makes FOUR great catches for Trent Rockets

Gregory said: "We were superb with the ball. We kept chipping away with important wickets. It was a little bit two-paced, with a bit of variable bounce at times. The bowling unit spoke about smashing the top of the stump as hard as we could.

"The guys up front with the bat have been outstanding. We're in a really good position, playing some fantastic cricket, and hopefully we can continue that."

Buttler become the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler hits a mega half century to win it for Manchester Super Giants vs Welsh Fire

After three straight defeats, Manchester Super Giants got the win they needed over Welsh Fire at an overcast Emirates Old Trafford to remain in contention for qualification.

Half-centuries from Tim Seifert and Jos Buttler propelling them to a crunching win with 31 balls to spare.

Seifert said: "We just tried to get off to a good start and maintain the run rate and it was good that we both got going. And it was quite nice to watch Buttler from the other end! We've got two big games ahead and this is a good little boost for us."

The Super Giants move up to 12 points, now just four behind the Fire with two games left each.

They had to do it without their captain Aiden Markram, who has returned to South Africa for personal reasons, Jos Buttler taking over captaincy duties and Paul Walter replacing him at the top of the order, meaning there were just three overseas players in the line-up.

Second-placed Fire won the toss and chose to bat, reaching an uncomfortable 4-0 from the first ten balls after Josh Tongue didn't concede a single run off his first five balls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leus du Plooy with a big drop catch for the Giants...

Spin was introduced at that stage, with Liam Dawson seeing Matt Short dropped almost immediately. The openers took full advantage, progressing steadily at first before opening up to reach 76 at the halfway stage. Their century partnership - the first in Fire men's history - came up after 70 balls.

Short was particularly severe on Noor Ahmad, who conceded 34 runs from 15 balls, while Sonny Baker was even more expensive. Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, however, were excellent, with the latter finally breaking the opening partnership at 125 after 83 balls by dismissing Phil Salt for 48. Short went on to make 71 from 47 balls, but with quick runs needed late on, Joe Root was not required at the crease as Fire posted what appeared to be a par score of 155, thanks largely to Rachin Ravindra's late cameo.

Sam Cook was unusually expensive with the ball as the Super Giants began their innings, with openers Tim Seifert and Paul Walter taking a liking to the pace of the Essex seamer, Chris Woakes and Lockie Ferguson as they raced to 53 without loss in the powerplay.

Walter went for 37 but the home side were 104-1 off 50, an extraordinary three no balls in six balls from Ferguson giving them a real boost.

Buttler started cautiously before switching into full attack mode, launching Marco Jansen into the stands to become the leading run-scorer in Twenty20 history, surpassing Kieron Pollard's tally of 14,803 runs. He celebrated the milestone by clearing the ropes in each of the next two balls, before adding further successive sixes to bring up a 20-ball half-century and guide his side home with ease.

Sports.title: Infantino remains FIFA president following crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had re-affirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events".

Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed plans to sell off a stake in the World Cup, which a number of associations said they had not been consulted on - with a deadline to back the proposals barely a month away in mid-September, with a £30.1m incentive to accept.

In a letter seen by Sky News sent to national associations and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, the pair wrote that they "sincerely apologised for the errors" around the proposals, which were withdrawn on Saturday after days of criticism from around world football.

In a second statement released on FIFA.com, the governing body hit back at its critics by defending its decision to withdraw the plans and said it would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

FIFA said it had "not been the intention… for member associations to feel excluded from the process" and admitted it should have been "handled differently", while promising a report would be presented at the next FIFA Council, comprising 37 representatives from around world football.

Infantino and FIFA had been criticised inside and outside of its own walls over the plans with Arsene Wenger, its chief of global football development, distancing himself publicly while Infantino's personal senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro quit his role on Friday, labelling the proposals a "bad deal" and "irresponsible".

The head of the Jordan FA went further by accusing Infantino of "blackmail", while UEFA announced it had "lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership" and the FA called for a "full and robust review of FIFA's leadership".

More to follow...

Sports.title: Castleford head coach Carr to miss the game against Hull KR
Sports.content:
Castleford Tigers head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game due to personal reasons.

Chris Chester, Scott Murrell and Rob Nickolay will lead the team in his absence and they will be supported by club legend and Man of Steel Adrian Vowles.

Australian Carr took charge in pre-season on a three-year deal having previously been coach of Featherstone Rovers and assistant manager at Leeds Rhinos in 2019.

A statement released by the club read: "Castleford Tigers RLFC can confirm that head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game this coming Friday. We can confirm that this is due to personal reasons, contrary to the reports on social media.

"In the interim, Chris Chester, Rob Nickolay and Scott Murrell will lead our on and off field operations. This leadership group will be heavily supported by Adrian Vowles and we thank Adrian for offering his support at short notice.

"We will not be making any other further comment at this stage, and we urge our fans to once again get behind our team this coming Friday."

Castleford currently sit ninth in the Super League table with seven wins from 21 games.

With six games remaining in the season, they face the Robins followed by Hull FC, St Helens, Catalans Dragons, Bradford Bulls, and Huddersfield Giants.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Arsenal beaten by Real Betis in Dublin friendly
Sports.content:
Arsenal produced a sloppy performance as they were beaten 3-1 by LaLiga side Real Betis in a pre-season friendly in Dublin.

The Gunners fell behind when Kepa Arrizabalaga came out and failed to claim a corner, allowing Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the back post. Nelson Deossa added a stunning second from long range.

Arsenal pulled one back when an inswinging corner from new signing Christos Tzolis was headed over the line by Piero Hincapie but Betis restored their two-goal lead when Pablo Fornals found the bottom corner following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz.

How did Arsenal line up? Starting XI: Kepa, White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri, Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis



Subbed on: Copley, Salmon, Gabriel, Vieira, Nelson, Jesus, Martinelli, Julienne, Meslier, Ibrahim, Ogunnaike, Clarke, Kabia, O'Neill

Mikel Arteta made second-half changes with Brazil internationals Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli given their first cameos of pre-season but Arsenal, still without Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and others involved at the World Cup, were unable to cut the deficit.

The defeat, their first of pre-season, comes as Arsenal continue to push for new signings in the transfer market, with the club having agreed a £75m fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes.

The key moments from Dublin

9 - GOAL! Kepa Arrizabalaga fails to claim a corner, allowing the unmarked Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the far post

Kepa Arrizabalaga fails to claim a corner, allowing the unmarked Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the far post 26 - GOAL! Nelson Deossa adds Real Betis's stunning second goal with a powerful long-range effort

Nelson Deossa adds Real Betis's stunning second goal with a powerful long-range effort 32 - GOAL! Christos Tzolis's inswinging corner loops over the Real Betis goalkeeper and is headed in by Piero Hincapie

Christos Tzolis's inswinging corner loops over the Real Betis goalkeeper and is headed in by Piero Hincapie 43 - GOAL! Pablo Fornals fires home a third goal for Real Betis following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz

Pablo Fornals fires home a third goal for Real Betis following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz 46 - SUBS! Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta makes seven half-time changes, with returning Brazilians Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli among those introduced

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta makes seven half-time changes, with returning Brazilians Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli among those introduced 55 - INJURY! Arsenal youngster Louie Copley is forced off with a serious-looking knee injury

Arsenal youngster Louie Copley is forced off with a serious-looking knee injury 64 - SAVE! Real Betis cut through Arsenal but Illan Meslier saves Isco's close-range flick

Real Betis cut through Arsenal but Illan Meslier saves Isco's close-range flick 67 - SHOT! Martinelli tees up a chance for Gabriel Jesus, who fires wide

Did Arsenal show need for Bruno?

With a lengthy list of players still to return following the World Cup, Arteta gave another chance to the midfield trio of Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri and Kai Havertz following the victory over Girona. This time, they found it more difficult.

Lewis-Skelly had some bright moments on the ball at No 6. He completed 70 of his 74 passes. But he couldn't provide the same level of defensive coverage of Rice, Martin Zubimendi, or indeed Guimaraes, whose move from Newcastle is getting closer.

Lewis-Skelly should still have a significant role to play for Arsenal this season. But Arsenal's struggles in midfield in Dublin showed why the club have pursued Guimaraes so aggressively. He will add elite quality and give Arsenal a level of depth their midfield currently lacks.

Of course, pre-season results count for little. This was primarily a fitness-building exercise for Arsenal. But their uncharacteristic openness leaves Arteta with food for thought right across the pitch as the Premier League champions prepare to defend their crown.

Image: Riccardo Calafiori challenges for the ball against Real Betis

Arteta: We didn't compete to our standards

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Premier Sports:

"Always upset when you lose a football match.

"Two very different halves, especially with the personnel we played today.

"The first half, we wanted two different things - play well and compete well. We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments. But the compete part, especially in and around our box, was not at our standards to win a football match against a good side.

"We have to have dominance. The first goal, the action from the corner, we concede a sloppy goal. Then we gave two giveaways very close to our box as well. They were very efficient, two very good goals as well from their side.

"It's always good when you lose a match in pre-season, it creates a bit more fire in the belly.

"It's better to give those goals away in a friendly match than an official match.

"It's a balance between understanding where we are and the personnel we are playing - and the demands that are at the highest level."

Arteta coy on Bruno arrival

Sports.title: Pakistan end eight-match away Test losing streak ahead of England clash
Sports.content:
Pakistan ended their eight-match away Test losing streak in emphatic fashion on Wednesday, securing an eight-wicket victory over the West Indies.

First innings century-maker Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam, in his first series since being reappointed as captain, led Pakistan to 77-2 with unbeaten knocks of 24 runs each as the visitors achieved victory shortly after lunch on day four and draw the series at 1-1.

Babar knocked off the target by hitting back-to-back sixes against left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican, whose six-wicket haul in the first innings had limited Pakistan's lead to 43 runs.

"You are always satisfied with the win," Babar said. "The most important thing was that we executed our plans whether it was how Abdullah Shafique batting or how the spinners bowled in the second innings."

Babar's decision to leave out his in-form fast bowler Mohammad Abbas in favour of extra spinner was vindicated as West Indies' batting crumbled against Pakistan's slow bowlers in the second innings.

"When we saw the pitch it looked more similar to how they are in Pakistan," Babar said. "We decided to play an additional spinner and it had an impact on our combinations because of which we had to leave out our senior players."

West Indies won the first Test by 90 runs in Tarouba, but Pakistan's spinners Sajid Khan and Ali Usman capitalised on favourable conditions on a wearing Queen's Park Oval pitch to help their side remain unbeaten in a Test series against West Indies since 2000.

Pakistan lost the wickets of Imam-ul-Haq, brilliantly snapped up by Justin Greaves in the slips cordon for nine in Jayden Seales' first over, and Azan Awais was bowled by Shamar Joseph for 18 before Shafique and Babar sealed the win inside four days.

West Indies opener Brandon King did not bat in the second innings after injuring his back on day three while pulling off a stunning direct-hit run-out of Babar from short cover.

Last recognised batter Justin Greaves fell for two after playing on to seamer Mohammad Ali, dragging a cross-batted shot onto his stumps via a thick inside edge.

British No 2 Cameron Norrie claimed a comfortable victory at the National Bank Open in Montreal to set up a third-round meeting with Katie Boulter's new husband Alex De Minaur.

Norrie, who snapped a six-match losing streak en route to the semi-finals in Los Cabos last week, followed up his opening win in Canada over Camilo Ugo Carabelli with more success against Peruvian Ignacio Buse.

Norrie, ranked four places below the Peruvian world No 33, secured a confident 6-3 6-3 win in one hour and 29 minutes.

The 30-year-old saved three out of the four break points he faced and converted four out of 11.

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, analyst Annabel Croft said: "Norrie was too experienced, too much game for his opponent. He applied the pressure when he needed to and defended extremely well with depth. We also saw him coming forward a lot, asking a lot of questions.
